catalog_quote: Ixcatec has three tones that contrast in word-final syllables: high (H), mid (M), and low (L). In non-final syllables, the contrast between mid and low tone is neutralized in favor of the mid tone (see DiCanio 2011 for a preliminary phonetic analysis of Ixcatec tone). Stress in Ixcatec typically falls on the penultimate syllable and is associated with increased duration and intensity and higher F0 (DiCanio 2012). ... unstressed vowels in Ixcatec typically have reduced duration, intensity and F0 relative to their stressed counterparts (DiCanio 2012). ... It should be noted that the coding for the variable STRESS was the same in the suffixed as in the unsuffixed forms since the suffix falls outside the domain of stress and thus does not trigger a rightward shift of stress from the penultimate syllable of the root. sources.quote: 'Ixcatec is a tone language, with three lexically contrastive tones ... Its phonology is complex and not yet well understood. The existence of stress is under discussion.' (same hedge as the held 2017 Cortypo sketches, repeated a year after the 2018 focus paper).

sources.quote: 'Hay una relación muy estrecha entre el tono y la intensidad. En general, todos los tonos van acompañados de cierta intensidad -más fuerte en los tonos altos y menor en los medios en contraste con los tonos bajos-, que es predecible y podemos interpretar como dos clases de acento: primario y secundario' with fn (a): 'Probablemente esta intensidad que percibimos en los tonos altos no exista en realidad; sino que la influencia de nuestra lengua nativa ... puede habernos hecho creer que en ixcateco existe acento ligado a los tonos altos.' sources.quote: No stress rule stated. Uses 'syllabe non accentuée' in passing for the initial syllables of disyllables ðiⁿgà/ðiⁿgi, which sits awkwardly with a penultimate-stress analysis; reports (after DiCanio, submitted) that low-tone vowel lengthening 'ne se produit jamais en position pénultième dans les polysyllabiques; par conséquent, la quantité vocalique est réduite en position non finale'.
sources.locator: intro note on transcription (three tone levels); sec. on class terms citing Miranda 1959 and DiCanio (soumis) for low-tone ban word-initially and vowel-length reduction in non-final position; sec. 4 remark that ð occurs 'presque toujours devant i en syllabe non accentuée' (exx. ðiⁿgà, ðiⁿgi, raðí, u-raðíⁿdʲà)
